questions.question: Compare natural, semi-synthetic, and synthetic antibiotics.
questions.solution_html:
• Compare natural, semi-synthetic, and synthetic antibiotics.
  • Natural antibiotics are produced directly by microorganisms such as bacteria and
  • fungi; examples include penicillin from Penicillium and streptomycin from
  • Streptomyces.
  • Semi-synthetic antibiotics are derived from natural antibiotics that are chemically
  • modified in the laboratory to improve their effectiveness, stability, or spectrum of
  • activity; examples include ampicillin and amoxicillin.
  • Synthetic antibiotics are entirely man-made through chemical synthesis, such as
  • sulfonamides and ciprofloxacin. While natural antibiotics are purely microbial
  • products, semi-synthetic ones combine natural and chemical methods, and
  • synthetic antibiotics are fully artificial, allowing greater control over their
  • properties and action.
questions.final_answer: properties and action
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: What is the principle of phase contrast microscopy?
questions.solution_html:
• CO2]
  • When light passes through cells, small phase shifts occur, which are invisible to the
  • human eye. In a phase-contrast microscope, these phase shifts are converted into
  • changes in amplitude, which can be observed as differences in image contrast.
questions.final_answer: changes in amplitude, which can be observed as differences in image contrast

questions.solution_html:

questions.question: Differentiate between F⁺ and F⁻ cells.
questions.solution_html:
• The F plasmid, or fertility plasmid, plays a crucial role in bacterial conjugation by
  • enabling the transfer of genetic material between bacteria. F+ cells, which contain
  • the entire F plasmid, act as donor cells. They form an F pilus, a structure that
  • connects to F- recipient cells, which lack the full F plasmid.

  • under steady-state conditions. A chemostat is a bioreactor in which fresh nutrient
  • medium is continuously added at a constant rate, while an equal volume of culture
  • is simultaneously removed.

questions.question: How R plasmids confer resistance to bacteria.
questions.solution_html:
• R plasmids make bacteria resistant by carrying genes that help destroy the antibiotic
  • block its entry, pump it out, or change the target site — allowing bacteria to survive

questions.question: What is the chemical composition of peptidoglycan?
questions.solution_html:
• A peptidoglycan monomer consists of two joined amino sugars, N-acetylglucosamine
  • (NAG) and N-acetylmuramic acid (NAM), with a pentapeptide coming off of the NAM.
  • In S. aureus, the pentapeptide consists of the amino acids L-alanine, D-glutamine, L
  • lysine, and two D-alanines.
questions.final_answer: Option (d) glutamine, L

questions.question: Explain the steps involved in specialized transduction.
questions.solution_html:
• Specialized transduction is a type of bacteriophage-mediated gene transfer in which
  • a specific portion of the bacterial DNA is transferred from one bacterium to another
  • through a temperate phage (such as lambda phage in E. coli).
  • Phage infects → integrates into host DNA (prophage)
  • Faulty excision → picks up nearby bacterial gene
  • New phage carries bacterial DNA → infects another cell
  • Gene recombines → genetic change in recipient
questions.final_answer: Gene recombines → genetic change in recipient
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Describe chemical agents of sterilization with examples.
questions.solution_html:
• Chemical agents of sterilization are chemical substances used to destroy or
  • eliminate all forms of microorganisms, including spores, on inanimate objects and
  • surfaces. They are used when heat or physical methods are not suitable.
  • Common examples include alcohols, aldehydes, ethylene oxide, halogens, phenols
  • and peroxides
questions.final_answer: and peroxides
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Write down the principle and procedure of Gram staining technique.
questions.solution_html:
• The Gram staining technique, developed by Hans Christian Gram in 1884, is used
  • to differentiate bacteria into two groups — Gram-positive and Gram-negative —
  • based on differences in their cell wall composition.
questions.final_answer: based on differences in their cell wall composition
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Describe the various techniques for isolation of pure cultures.
questions.solution_html:
• CO3]
  • A pure culture may be isolated by the use of special media with specific
  • chemical or physical agents that allow the enrichment or selection of one
  • organism over another. Pure culture isolation techniques such as streak
  • plate, pour plate, spread plate, serial dilution, and enrichment culture help
  • separate individual microbial species from mixed populations for study and
  • identification.
questions.final_answer: identification
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Write notes on transport media with examples.
questions.solution_html:
• Transport media are those culture media that are used to maintain the
  • viability of pathogenic microorganisms present in a clinical sample and to
  • prevent the potential pathogens to be overgrown by other commensals or
  • contaminants in the specimen during the transportation of the clinical
  • specimen to the clinical/diagnostic laboratory.
  • Examples: Stuart’s medium, Amies medium, Cary–Blair medium, and Viral
  • Transport Medium.
questions.final_answer: Transport Medium
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Write a short note on the industrial applications of yeast.
questions.solution_html:
• Yeast has several crucial industrial applications. Important examples
  • include: Baking Industry: Used as a leavening agent to make bread, cakes
  • and other bakery products rise. Brewing Industry: Essential for the
  • fermentation process that produces alcoholic beverages like beer and wine.
